LESSON MENU
CLOCKED RS FLIP-FLOP
The Clocked RS flip-flop is designed to store the last input condition until the next input condition is gated through.
DISCUSSION
Clocked RS flip-flops have three inputs and two outputs.
A high applied to the S input sets the output state to a high Q, low Q when the clock (C) input is high.
A high applied to the R input sets the output states to a high Q, low Q when the clock input is high.
When the clock input is low, the S and R inputs are disabled and the flip-flop stays in its current state.
The Clocked RS flip-flop is a good replacement for the mechanical switch.
The light is on when the clock and S inputs are high.
When would this Clocked RS flip-flop produce a high Q output? ???
A high input on R and a high clock on C produces a Q output.....
TRY AGAIN!
A low on C disables the S and R inputs. The output state of the flip-flop will not change.
TRY AGAIN!
This clocked RS flip-flop is constructed from four NAND gates. Clocked RS flip-flops may also beconstructed from NOR gates.
This clocked RS flip-flop is constructed from four NAND gates. Clocked RS flip-flops may also be constructed from NOR gates.
Note that gates C and D form a simple NAND RS flip-flop...
Adding gates A and B and a clock input makes this circuit a Clocked NAND RS flip-flop.
Let's start the discussion with the flip-flop in the SET or Q high output state.
Trace the inputs through gates A and B. The outputs are S = 0 and R =1.
Trace the inputs through gates A and B. The outputs are S = 0 and R =1.
Definition
The high output from gate C is used as feedback to gate D. The output of gate D is low.
The low output from gate D is used as feedback to gate C. The output of gate C is high.
When the clock is low the outputs from gates A and B are high. The two high inputs to gate D still produce a low output. The flip-flop stays in its current state.
The clock input must be high to change the flip-flop's state.
Now trace the inputs through gates A and B. The outputs are S=1 and R=0.
The output of NAND gate D becomes high because at least one input is low. This high is fed back to gate C. The output of gate C becomes low.
This Clocked RS flip-flop is now in a high Q or RESET state.
What is the output state of this Clocked RS flip-flop?
Trace the high applied to S and C inputs through gates A and C. The low applied to gate C is inverted to a high and applied to Q.
TRY AGAIN!
What is the output state of this SET Clocked RS flip-flop?
The flip-flop is in the SET state. With the Clock input LOW, the state will not change with a HIGH input on R.
TRY AGAIN!
This completes the information on CLOCKED RS FLIP-FLOP.....

3. A high applied to the R and C inputs sets Q low and Q high.

CLOCKED RS FLIP-FLOP

This experiment demonstrates the operation of a Clocked RS flip-flop. You will enter input signals for SET, RESET and CLOCK and probe the outputs of the flip-flop to verify the correct output signals at Q and Q.signals.m
EXPERIMENT
Pick up the PC130-128 card. The purpose of this card is to demonstrate the operation of a Clocked RS flip-flop.
Switches S1 and S2 are used to apply the SET or RESET input signals. Placing the switches to the 1 position applies +5 volts to the circuit.
The PC130-111 Clock/Pulser Card is used to supply the clock input to the flip-flop.
With PC130-111 S2 in the clock position, a continuous train of pulses are applied to the flip-flop on PC130-128.
With PC130-111 S2 in the pulser position, a pulse is applied to the flip-flop on PC130-128 only when S1 on PC130-111 is pressed.
Note on PC130-128, gates C and D are shown as inhibited OR gates.
The logic output of an inhibited OR gate is the same as a NAND gate. Let's begin the experiment.
